implementation_notes: Header-only library realization: one signal per event type is the hub, slots are lambdas or function objects, and connection objects (or scoped_connection) provide the unsubscribe handle. Managed connections track subscriber lifetime, which removes the classic dangling-callback bug; prefer this default when Boost is acceptable and the fan-out is in-process.
pitfalls: Slots execute synchronously in the emitting thread; heavy work inside a slot blocks the publisher and all later slots.
A signal destroyed while emitting has undefined behaviour - keep the hub alive for the lifetime of its publishers, e.g. as a long-lived service object.

variants.name: Qt QObject signals and slots
variants.idiom_name: QObject hub with one signal per event + QObject::connect
variants.implementation_notes: Framework realization: the hub is a QObject subclass whose signals are the channels, subscribers are slots connected with function-pointer syntax (compile-time checked) and connections are removed automatically when sender or receiver is destroyed. Choose it inside a Qt application, where the meta-object system and the event loop already exist; Qt 6 requires C++17, Qt 5 only C++11.
pitfalls: A queued connection needs an event loop and marshals the payload through the meta-type system, so custom payload types must be registered with qRegisterMetaType.
Lambdas connected without a context object are not disconnected automatically - pass the receiver as context to keep Qt's lifetime management.
Signals must be emitted from the thread that owns the receiver or via a queued connection; direct connections from other threads race the receiver's data.
